questions.question: A toy boat is pulled northwards with a force of 12 N by a string, while the water current pushes it southwards with a force of 4 N, and the wind blows it southwards with a force of 3 N. What is the resultant force on the boat?
options: 19 N Northwards
5 N Northwards
5 N Southwards
9 N Northwards

questions.question: A sledge is pulled to the right with a force of 45 N by a child, while a friction force of 30 N acts to the left. In which direction will the resultant force act, and why?
options: To the right, because the pulling force is greater than the friction force.
To the left, because friction always overcomes pulling forces.
It will not act in any direction because the forces are balanced.
To the right, because the sledge is already moving to the right.

questions.question: Four identical toy cars (A, B, C, and D) are pushed along a frictionless track with different resultant forces. Car A has a resultant force of 2 N, Car B has 5 N, Car C has 1.5 N, and Car D has 4 N. Which car's speed will change most rapidly?
options: Car C
Car A
Car D
Car B

questions.question: A raised heavy hammer has gravitational potential energy store. In physics terms, what does having this energy store fundamentally mean for the hammer before it is released?
options: It contains a physical fluid called energy that will spill out upon impact.
It possesses properties that allow it to interact with and cause changes to a nail when dropped.
It is guaranteed to stay suspended indefinitely without any external support.
It has lost its mass and became pure force ready to do work.

questions.question: A student slides a heavy wooden block across a smooth ice rink and then across a concrete playground with the same initial push. Why does the block stop much sooner on the concrete?
options: Concrete exerts a larger gravitational pull on the block than ice does.
The concrete surface provides a much larger friction force that opposes and slows down the block's movement.
The block's mass decreases as it slides on concrete, reducing its forward momentum.
Air resistance is significantly higher over concrete surfaces than over ice.

questions.question: At a microscopic level, even highly polished metal sheets have tiny bumps and ridges. How does this microscopic structure explain the origin of friction when two such sheets slide over each other?
options: The microscopic ridges interlock and collide, resisting the relative movement between the surfaces.
The ridges create pocket vacuums that suck the two sheets together.
The air trapped between the ridges acts as a strong glue.
The rough ridges generate electrostatic repulsion that pushes the plates apart.

questions.question: A bicycle chain is squeaking and stiff. After applying a thin layer of oil, the pedals turn much more easily. Which statement best explains how the oil achieved this effect?
options: The oil reacts chemically with the metal to make the chain lighter.
The oil fills the microscopic gaps and separates the rough surfaces, reducing the friction between them.
The oil increases the contact area to increase the grip between the chain and the gears.
The oil acts as an adhesive that binds the chain links tightly together.

questions.question: A student notices that when a newton meter is hanging empty, the pointer rests at the 0.5 N mark instead of 0 N. If they use this meter to measure a 4.0 N weight without adjusting it, what will the scale read, and how should they fix this?
options: It will read 3.5 N; they should subtract 0.5 N from all readings.
It will read 4.5 N; they should adjust the zero calibration screw to align the pointer with 0 N before measuring.
It will read 4.5 N; they must buy a new meter as this one is permanently damaged.
It will read 4.0 N; the error automatically corrects itself when a load is added.

questions.question: A student wants to measure a force that they estimate to be around 2.4 N. They have three newton meters available: Meter X (range 0–1 N, divisions of 0.1 N), Meter Y (range 0–5 N, divisions of 0.1 N), and Meter Z (range 0–100 N, divisions of 5 N). Which meter is the most appropriate choice?
options: Meter X, because it has the smallest divisions and will be highly precise.
Meter Z, because its large scale ensures it will not break under any circumstances.
Meter Y, because its scale accommodates the force and offers detailed divisions for an accurate reading.
Either Meter Y or Meter Z, as the total range of the meter does not affect readability.

questions.question: A group of students tests how much force is needed to slide a wooden block across different floor coverings: carpet, vinyl, wood, and concrete. What type of chart should they use to display their results, and why?
options: A line graph, because both the floor covering and the force are continuous variables.
A bar chart, because the independent variable (type of floor covering) is categoric.
A scatter graph, because there are multiple trials for each floor type.
A pie chart, because they need to show the proportion of total force used on each floor.

questions.question: To investigate how the surface area of a parachute affects its fall time, students drop parachutes of different sizes. To ensure this is a fair test, what must they do regarding the variables?
options: Change both the surface area and the mass of the parachutes at the same time.
Change only the surface area of the parachute, keeping all other variables like mass and drop height the same.
Keep the surface area constant and change the material of each parachute.
Change the drop height for each different parachute size.

questions.question: A student measures the friction force of a shoe on wood three times, getting results of 4.2 N, 4.1 N, and 8.9 N. What is the value of repeating this measurement, and how should they handle the 8.9 N result?
options: It confirms all results are reliable, so they should calculate the mean of all three values.
It helps identify the 8.9 N reading as an anomaly, which should be investigated and excluded before calculating the mean.
It shows that the shoe grew heavier during the third test, so the third reading is the most accurate.
It proves that the equipment is broken, so they should discard all results and start a different experiment.

questions.question: A magnet is held 2 cm above a steel paperclip, causing the paperclip to jump up and stick to the magnet. Which statement correctly describes the magnetic force during this event?
options: It is a contact force because the paperclip eventually touches the magnet.
It is a non-contact force because it pulled the paperclip upwards before they were touching.
It is only a force once the physical contact is established.
It is a contact force that acts through the air molecules pushing the paperclip.

questions.question: A skydiver is falling through the air before opening their parachute. What is the nature of the drag force acting on the skydiver?
options: It is a non-contact force of gravity pulling the skydiver upwards.
It is a contact force caused by the skydiver's body colliding with and pushing through air particles.
It is an electromagnetic force field generated by the rapid motion.
It is a constant downward force that increases their speed of descent.

questions.question: In a force diagram of a rising hot air balloon, the upward thrust arrow is drawn 6 cm long, while the downward gravity arrow is drawn 4 cm long. What do these lengths tell us about the forces?
options: The downward force of gravity is larger because it is more concentrated.
The upward thrust force is larger than the downward gravity force.
Both forces are equal because they are acting on the same balloon.
The balloon is moving horizontally because the arrows have different lengths.

questions.question: A book rests quietly on a wooden table. How should the upward support force acting on the book be labeled according to scientific standards?
options: The force acting on the table by the book.
The force acting on the book by gravity.
The force acting on the book by the table.
The force acting on the table by the floor.

questions.question: Two grocery trolleys are in a supermarket. Trolley X is empty, while Trolley Y is fully loaded with heavy canned goods. Why is Trolley Y much harder to suddenly turn around a corner than Trolley X?
options: Trolley Y has a greater mass, so it requires a greater force to change its direction of motion.
Trolley Y experiences less friction from the floor, making it slide out of control.
Trolley X has more chemical energy, which assists the shopper in steering it.
Trolley Y is subject to a stronger magnetic field from the floor.

questions.question: A tennis ball is flying through the air. In which of the following situations is a force NOT being applied to the ball?
options: The ball hits the racket, causing it to compress and change shape.
The ball strikes the court surface and bounces upward, changing its direction.
The ball continues to fly in a straight line at a completely constant speed in deep, empty space.
The ball slows down as it travels through the air due to air resistance.

questions.question: A cyclist travels along a straight, flat road. The forward force from their pedaling is exactly 40 N, and the backward drag force is exactly 40 N. Which of the following describes the cyclist's motion?
options: The cyclist will gradually slow down and eventually come to a stop.
The cyclist will continue moving forward at a constant speed because there is no resultant force.
The cyclist will instantly stop moving because the forces cancel out.
The cyclist will accelerate forward because the pedaling force was applied first.

questions.question: An archer pulls back a bowstring, bending the bow. In terms of energy and forces, what is happening during this process?
options: The force applied by the archer's hands transfers energy into the elastic store of the bow by changing its shape.
Energy is destroyed by the force of friction as the string moves backward.
The bow creates new energy because of the tension force within its material.
No energy is transferred because the bow is not yet moving through the air.
